name: צוּעָר
summary: A man of Issachar, named only as the father of Nethanel, the tribe’s leader in the wilderness, who stood with Moses at the census, brought Issachar’s offering on the second day and led its company when the camp set out from Sinai. The name is a noun of the root of צָעִיר “little, younger”, in the same qutāl pattern as Akkadian ṣuḫāru “boy”: “little one”, perhaps given to a younger son.

evidence.note: “Of Issachar, Nethanel the son of צוּעָר”: among the men who stood with Moses and Aaron.
Nethanel son of Zuar, leader of Issachar, camping beside Judah.
On the second day Nethanel son of Zuar presented Issachar’s offering.
Over the company of the tribe of Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar, when the camp set out.
The root’s adjective: “the youngest (הַצָּעִיר) according to his youth”.
“I am the צָּעִיר in my father’s house”: the little one of a family.

note: The form צוּעָר is not otherwise a word in scripture; “little one” rests on the root’s adjective and on Akkadian ṣuḫāru, the same pattern. The Septuagint spells it Σωγαρ, with γ for the ġ behind ע.
